clue.text: Listening with both ears!

parts.note: the whole clue simply describes the way someone hears when sound reaches each side of the head at once, the exclamation flagging a straightforward cryptic description

explanation.surface: An exclamation about paying full attention, ears on both sides tuned in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin bin- means two and aural relates to hearing, so this adverb describes hearing through a pair of organs.

clue.text: Fancy a little house beside a lake

annotationWithheld.why: Fancy a little house beside a lake (4): no parse gives IDEA from 'a little house beside a lake'; the clue as held seems wrong for its answer and no source gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: Fancy a little house beside a lake

clue.text: Accepts it's mad to get upset

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that it is crazy to become distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get upset' rearranges ITSMAD, the letters of 'it's mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge or grant something is to accept it.

clue.text: A building one may be shown round

definitions.text: A building one may be shown round

parts.words: A building one may be shown round
parts.note: the surface suggests a guided tour, but round means the building itself is circular in shape

explanation.surface: A building where visitors may be given a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular building, often domed, is literally a round structure.

clue.text: Fat boy-about right

indicators.note: about means the boy goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that a plump lad has it about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered pig fat used in cooking is a kind of fat.

clue.text: Hankered for months to join Edward

parts.note: a year is a span of twelve months
Ned is a familiar form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone longed for months to join a man named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To long or pine for something is to hanker after it.

clue.text: Still with nothing to argue about?

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put forward for debate
the suffix less means having none, being without

explanation.surface: A question whether a quiet person simply has nothing to dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a debate with no proposal tabled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoving or stationary, so still.

clue.text: The copy writer

parts.note: a copywriter writes advertising text, but here the writer literally copies another's work and passes it off as their own

explanation.surface: A job title for someone writing advertising text.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary thief who passes off others' words as their own is a writer who copies.

clue.text: Game reserves

definitions.meaning: a cue sport played on a table with pockets, like billiards
a shared fund or stock that several parties draw upon

explanation.surface: A note about land kept aside for wild animals and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pocket-table cue sport and a common fund of resources held jointly.

clue.text: Where the young are raised by social crawlers

definitions.text: Where the young are raised by social crawlers

parts.words: Where the young are raised by social crawlers
parts.note: the social crawlers are colony-living insects, and the place their young are raised is the mound-like nest they build

explanation.surface: A description that sounds like a parenting guide for socialites who crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the plural of a nest mound built by white ants, where a colony rears its brood.

clue.text: Deserving severe criticism

definitions.meaning: as in a story 'meriting a mention', being worthy of something
a scolding or telling-off, from the old verb rate, to berate

explanation.surface: A remark that someone has earned a harsh dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means meriting (it was worth a mention) and also a stern reprimand, from rate meaning scold.

clue.text: A coastal area some choose as ideal for retirement

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a place by the sea where people like to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals a run of letters inside 'choose as ideal'; 'for retirement' is surface dressing tying the beach to pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of land beside the sea, a resort coast, is a coastal area.

clue.text: Priests eat hash-there's an entertaining revelation!

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to jumble it, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Clergymen eating a stew provide a surprising spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hash' rearranges PRIESTSEAT, the letters of 'Priests eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A show of gradual undressing reveals the performer, an entertainment of exposure.

clue.text: A record in lyric form expressing contrition

indicators.note: in puts the record inside the poetic word

parts.note: lyric verse is a poetic form
a log is a written record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: A sorry message delivered as a verse recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry and saying so, as in an apology, is expressing contrition.

clue.text: An occasion demanding uniform with a casual sort of shirt

parts.note: even means level or uniform
a T-shirt is a casual top, giving T

explanation.surface: A function that requires uniform, though a T-shirt is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening or function is an occasion.

clue.text: Tie up an untidy plant

indicators.note: untidy suggests the letters of the preceding words are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction to stake up a straggly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges TIEUPAN, the letters of 'Tie up an'.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower with trumpet-shaped blooms, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Getting in a top journalist after political leader faded

indicators.note: after puts the chosen leading letter ahead of what follows
the leader of the word political is its first letter

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist

explanation.surface: A top reporter is recruited after a politician's career faded.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine away is to waste or wither, so to fade.

clue.text: A five ring one, many keep away

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
a ring is O-shaped
I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A head count at some gathering where a few phone and most stay away.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or steer clear of something is to keep away from it.

clue.text: Overcharge for a bird

definitions.meaning: to swindle or fleece a customer

explanation.surface: A complaint that a pet shop charged too much for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to cheat by charging too much, and it is also a black crow that nests in colonies.

clue.text: Topping military gear!

parts.note: topping here is literal, the item of uniform worn on top of the head, while the surface reads as praise for excellent kit

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cry that some army kit is splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A French military cap with a flat circular top and peak, worn on the head.

clue.text: Poles always looking derisory

parts.note: S and N are the abbreviations for the south and north poles
e'er is a poetic contraction meaning ever, always

explanation.surface: A comment that Polish people always seem scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: A scornful facial expression, a curled lip, is a derisive look.

clue.text: He's paid for sorting letters

indicators.note: sorting means the letters of the word are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A postal worker is paid to sort mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting' rearranges the letters of 'letters'. One who has settled up, i.e. paid, is a settler.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill is to pay it, so the one who settles is the one who has paid.

clue.text: Comes to and feels the pain again

definitions.meaning: arrives at a place or a total

explanation.surface: Someone recovers consciousness and the agony returns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means arrives at, and split as re-aches it means hurts a second time.

clue.text: Support the developer, a man of vision

parts.note: a prop is something that holds up or supports

indicators.note: the word the is developed, i.e. worked into a new shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: An appeal to back a property developer as a visionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developer' makes HET from the letters of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer who foretells the future is someone with visions.

clue.text: Place to put money away

definitions.meaning: to set or lay something down
to pay funds into a bank account

explanation.surface: A question about where to stash savings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means both to set down and to lodge cash in a bank.

clue.text: Thought love 15 down

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the answer to 15 down, meaning faded

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue saying love has withered.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a view or express an opinion is to have thought something.

clue.text: Actors off-stage

parts.note: the stage direction in a script telling several players to leave, Latin for they go out

explanation.surface: A note about performers resting in the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for they go out, it is the script direction for players leaving the stage.

clue.text: Ruler of an ancient kingdom and of sporting association

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, which governs English football

explanation.surface: A monarch from history also linked with a sports body.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was the eighth-century king of Mercia, of Offa's Dyke fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical English king who governed the Anglo-Saxon realm of Mercia.

clue.text: Quarters on a ship for the head

parts.note: N and E are compass points, the quarters of the compass
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Cabins on a vessel reserved for the captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, a promontory, not the ship's toilet the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland or promontory, as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness, is a coastal head.

clue.text: Having sinister propensity

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, so the leaning is a preference for one hand rather than a wicked bent

explanation.surface: A description of someone inclined towards evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister originally meant on the left side, so favouring that hand is the sinister propensity.

clue.text: Get clear of the inexperienced motorist in drink!

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter inside the drink

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls
L is for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of a learner driver who has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the slip is to escape or get away from them.

clue.text: Dries hops a new way — speak with great enthusiasm of it

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a new way, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A brewer gushing about a novel method of drying hops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new way' rearranges DRIESHOPSA, the letters of 'Dries hops a'; the second 'a' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush or wax lyrical is to talk with great enthusiasm.
